stories.title: Former Cowboys DB, Broncos scout Cornell Green dies at 86
stories.summary: The Cowboys announced that former defensive back Cornell Green died Wednesday.
stories.detail: The Cowboys announced that former defensive back Cornell Green died Wednesday . He was 86. Green grew up in California as an elite basketball player, earning all-start honors. He went to Utah State, where he earned All-America honors in 1961 and '62. His 1,067 rebounds still stand as the school's career record, and he is Utah State's sixth-leading scorer with 1,890 points. He had planned to join the NBA after the Chicago Zephyrs drafted him in 1962, but the Cowboys offered Green an invite to training camp. Despite only one year of football experience — his junior year of high school — Green made the Cowboys' roster. Green never missed a game over the next 13 seasons, starting 167 of 168 games after his rookie season. He played cornerback his first eight seasons. Green led the Cowboys in interceptions four times, earned three Pro Bowl invites and garnered two first-team All-Pro honors. In 1970, Green moved to safety, where he was named a Pro Bowler again in 1971 and '72. He played in two NFL Championship Games and Super Bowl V before helping the Cowboys win the Lombardi Trophy with a 24-3 victory over the Dolphins in Super Bowl VI. First off, the Cowboys are still very much in the playoff race due to the poor state of the NFC East division. stories.title: Panthers LB Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) set to miss Week 7 game vs. Bucs
stories.summary: Panthers coach Dave Canales said the team is preparing to host the Buccaneers on Sunday without top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips.
stories.detail: CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- Carolina Panthers coach Dave Canales said Wednesday the team is preparing to host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday without top outside linebacker Jaelan Phillips . Canales didn't offer a timeline for Phillips (hamstring) to return, but he avoided any gamesmanship on Phillips' status for Week 7. When asked if the expectation was that Phillips would miss this week, with a Thursday Night Football matchup against the Green Bay Packers on deck for Week 8, Canales noted that Phillips, who reinjured his left injury hamstring in the win over the Philadelphia Eagles , needed to be treated with caution. "I think I can fairly say that," Canales said about Phillips missing Week 7. "I know there are advantages to game plans, but this is something that we need to address and take care of." Phillips left Sunday's win in the first half but returned late in the third quarter. On Wednesday, Phillips walked around the perimeter of the Panthers' practice field while his teammates participated in a walkthrough. stories.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson returns to practice but status remains unclear vs. Bengals
stories.summary: After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp.
stories.detail: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson returned to practice Wednesday, but it remains uncertain whether the two-time NFL Most Valuable Player will play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . After practice, Jackson was favoring his injured left ankle, walking into the team facility with a noticeable limp. He also walked with a limp inside the locker room. Jackson wasn't present during the media availability portion of practice, but he later came out onto the practice field. This marked the first time that Jackson has had any on-field work since spraining his ankle 17 days ago. Ravens coach Jesse Minter described Jackson as a limited participant, saying he "was able to get in a little bit of work and be involved in preparation." Minter also indicated Jackson participated in some team drills. "There's nobody that wants to be out there more than Lamar," Minter said. "Lamar wants to play. But at the same time, you got to be healthy enough to play." Jackson sprained his left ankle late in the first half of a 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans on Oct. 4. stories.title: Jameis Winston on losing his starting job: I understand where I am now
stories.summary: The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J.
stories.detail: The Giants benched Jameis Winston just 23 days after trading with the Vikings for J.J. McCarthy. McCarthy will become the third quarterback to start for the Giants, following Jaxson Dart and Winston. Dart tore the MCL and meniscus in his left knee in Week 2, ending his season. Winston started the past four games, going 2-1-1. He was only 14-of-26 for 152 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions on Sunday, leaving with the Giants trailing 34-10 in the fourth quarter. McCarthy rallied the team, going 11-of-21 for 243 yards, a touchdown and an interception and gave the Giants a chance for a miracle comeback. That's why Winston accepts returning to a backup role. "Last game it wasn’t what it was capble of being," Winston said, via video from SNY Giants. "Every single week, you're defined off of the last time you stepped foot on the field. So I believe based off last game, my job is to lead the New York Football Giants to a win, and that didn't happen. That being said, I understand where I am now." stories.title: Sources: Warriors exploring options to trade center Kristaps Porzingis
stories.summary: The Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
stories.detail: The Golden State Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis , who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has him seriously contemplating his future in basketball, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The Warriors released a statement Wednesday saying they were "not going to comment on trade speculation or reports regarding his health-related matter or future." Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the team in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million in the second season is guaranteed, essentially making it an expiring contract. The front office strategically designed the extension without a raise between the two seasons, keeping him immediately trade-eligible instead of needing to wait until mid-December. Despite the built-in flexibility, that wasn't the idealized intent of the contract. Porzingis played in 15 of the team's final 20 games last season, and the Warriors' management believed he had an encouraging enough summer to pencil Porzingis in as the projected starting center next to Draymond Green and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg in the frontcourt. stories.title: Sources: Mavericks agree to two-way deal with Walter Clayton Jr.
stories.summary: The Mavericks agree to a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN.
stories.detail: The Dallas Mavericks have agreed on a two-way NBA deal with former first-round pick Walter Clayton Jr., sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Wednesday. Clayton was waived earlier this week by the Memphis Grizzlies ahead of the league's roster cut-down deadline. He is joining the Mavericks after clearing waivers. Memphis acquired Clayton from Utah on Feb. 3 in the eight-player trade that sent Jaren Jackson Jr ., Jock Landale , John Konchar and Vince Williams Jr. to the Jazz. Clayton played 24 games for the Grizzlies last season after the trade, averaging 9.7 points, 2.1 rebounds and 5.7 assists and shooting 36.6% from 3-point range. Clayton, 23, was the No. 18 pick in the 2025 draft after helping Florida win its third national title. He was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player and was a consensus first-team All-American in 2025. The Mavericks, still light on ball handlers despite the return of Kyrie Irving from his ACL injury, could use the depth Clayton provides in their backcourt.

stories.title: The Warriors’ terrible Kristaps Porzingis news is a problem without a viable solution
stories.summary: Kristaps Porzingis’ diagnosis is terrible news for the Warriors.
stories.detail: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Would you believe that Kristaps Porzingis graded out as one of the better players in the NBA last season? It’s true. Porzingis ranked No. 50 in the league in Estimated Plus-Minus and nearly cracked the top-25 in LEBRON, which are a pair of metrics that measure a player’s impact with some luck adjustments and player tracking data built in . Every all-in-one stat is going to have blindspots and needs to be taken with a large grain of salt, but both teams Porzingis played for last season — the Atlanta Hawks and Golden State Warriors — were much better with him on the court in his 32 total games, and that’s no coincidence. Porzingis showed the whole world how good he could be on the Boston Celtics’ run to the 2024 NBA championship, when his combination of outside shooting and rim protection made him the rare center who could space the floor to the max without giving much back on defense. Porzingis’ effectiveness hasn’t been much of a question since his career-defining season in Boston, but his availability has been. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images I don’t think I was ready for the season to start. After that car crash of a series in June where we watched the Spurs’ magical run go up in flames, I just shut everything down. I simply did my best not to think about it. I tried watching baseball. I tried going outside. It’s not “repressing your feelings” if you’re doing it in a healthy way, right? And it worked. Mostly. I spent the whole summer without rage baiting myself with clips of the OG’s tip-in or Knicks fans dancing around in our building. I didn’t watch the draft. I didn’t follow the offseason.
